title: Server route mounts and middleware order (server.ts)

title: authenticateUser runs once per /api/projects mount traversed (5 to 9 Supabase Auth calls per request)
summary: authenticateUser reads the Bearer token and calls supabase.auth.getUser(token) with the service-role client, which is a network round trip to Supabase Auth per call. Because the same middleware is passed to each /api/projects router mount, a request that matches a later router passes through every earlier mount's middleware. Matching checkout routes runs 6 validations; matching sceneStageLocks routes runs 9. Requests with no Bearer header return 401 before any network call.
notes: Multiplicity follows Express app.use semantics (a middleware runs for every matching layer that calls next). Count per route family is derived from mount order, not measured at runtime.

title: video_generation_jobs lifecycle, auto-retry (3 attempts) and manual retry
summary: confirm-render inserts queued rows (one per shot with a start frame URL) and then fires the global executor. The executor moves a job to processing (processing_started_at), increments attempt_count with a separate write, then generating, uploading (provider_job_id recorded after the provider already uploaded) and completed (video_url, storage_path, actual_cost, completed_at). On failure, if the attempt count is below max_retries (default 3) it goes back to queued with error_message; otherwise it goes to failed. Manual retry only accepts failed rows, sets queued and clears error and provider fields but leaves attempt_count, so a retried job gets one attempt. The retryable flag on provider errors is ignored.

title: Global in-process video executor loop (serial, memory flag, no row claim, no startup hook)
summary: A single VideoJobExecutor instance holds an in-memory isProcessing flag. processQueuedJobs loops: select the oldest queued row across all users (fetchNextQueuedJob), process it, sleep 500 ms, repeat. A second trigger while running is a no-op, but the running loop keeps polling and picks up new rows. There is no row lock or conditional claim (select by status queued, then update by id only). DB errors in the fetch are treated as an empty queue. Any exception escaping processJob (for example a failed status write in the failure branch) ends the loop and leaves the job in its last written status. Nothing calls processQueuedJobs at startup, and pollIntervalMs is declared but unused.

title: Error handling: route-level catch and JSON responses; global handler reached only via next(err)
summary: Routes handle errors inline: 214 catch blocks and roughly 327 res.status(500) responses across route files, most returning the error message. The global errorHandler is reached only through next(err), which in this codebase happens for body-parser failures (malformed JSON, oversize body) and synchronous throws; the only other next() call is authenticateUser's success path. title: All background work lives in the API process; no recovery exists for non-terminal rows

title: No concurrency limit on image or video provider calls beyond the serial video loop
summary: Each image job request spawns an unawaited executeJobInBackground with no semaphore, queue, or per-user limit, so parallel Gemini image calls scale with request volume (the only limit is the 4-attempt retry inside the client). Video calls are serial per process, and their submit and poll share the same loop, so one slow Veo job blocks all queued videos for every user.
notes: Grep for p-limit, semaphore, concurren, mutex, pLimit, maxConcurrent, rateLimit in backend/src (non-test) returned no matches.

title: Retry and manual retry cannot dedupe or limit spend (charged jobs re-run without a cap)
summary: Auto-retry re-runs the full paid provider call up to three times for every error class, including PERMANENT safety-filter or bad-model errors that the provider classified as non-retryable. Manual retry of a failed Veo job runs one more paid call with no credit check, no charge recording, and no attempt reset. Duplicate confirm-render also re-queues and re-charges the whole scene with no existing-job check.
notes: Charge and provider spend per failed attempt are inferred from the provider call structure (Veo bills per generation under the design of the call); billing terms are external and not verified.

title: Client timeouts end before server work does, and the UI loops never end on stranded states
summary: Client budgets for image jobs (60 to 120 seconds) end before the server has any deadline, so the UI can show a timeout while the job continues and later writes the asset. Conversely, Stage 10 and Stage 12 loops poll with no ceiling and continue forever on stranded frames or jobs. Server-side, Veo has a 5-minute poll cap, and the video retry loop can then resubmit a paid job up to three times.
notes: Veo timeout returns TEMPORARY (Veo3Provider.ts:296-298), which the executor retries as a fresh paid submission.

summary: Shot extraction asks the model for an optional array of strings named continuity_flags and stores it on shots. The only logic that reads it is determineContinuityLink, which forces the continuity mode to none when a flag matches cut, jump, transition, time-skip, new-scene or later. No structured handoff, entry, exit or prop-exchange flag exists.
notes: Shot-level continuity_flags is not the same field as transformation_flags. The regex is case-insensitive and matches substrings, so a flag such as 'later' also matches phrases unrelated to scene breaks.

title: Veo3 request hardcodes audio, person, resize and sample settings; no negative prompt, seed, resolution or audio toggle
summary: Veo3Provider sends generateAudio true, personGeneration allow_adult, resizeMode pad and sampleCount 1, takes aspectRatio from the project, and sends only prompt plus start image and optional lastFrame. No negativePrompt, seed, resolution or per-request audio setting is passed. ImageProviderInterface declares negativePrompt and seed, but the only generateImage call (ImageGenerationService) sets neither.
notes: Veo branch runs only when VIDEO_PROVIDER=veo3 (default is mock). Runtime provider behaviour is UNKNOWN statically.

title: LLM prompt output is hard-sliced to 1200 or 500 characters with a trailing ellipsis
summary: cleanPromptOutput cuts any output longer than maxLength to maxLength-3 characters and appends '...'. Frame, end-frame, continuity and correction prompts use 1200; video prompts use 500. The video template lists SOUND DESIGN as the fourth and last part, so a long output can lose its audio section; no warning or retry is raised.
notes: Extends wave-1 FACT-0115, which records the limits but not the silent cut or its effect on the audio section. Effect on generated content is UNKNOWN statically.

title: Compatible-model tags include Runway Gen-3 and Kling with no integration; tags are persisted and never read by the UI
summary: determineCompatibleModels always returns Veo3, adds 'Runway Gen-3' when the frame prompt is 500 characters or less and the shot has no dialogue, and adds 'Kling' when duration is 10 seconds or less. generate-prompts persists the list to shots.compatible_models. No file under src/ references compatibleModels or compatible_models.
notes: Tags are informational; no video call is routed to either model.

title: Stage 12 unsatisfied-issue routing has no path back to Stage 10 frames
summary: UnsatisfiedDropdown maps visual-continuity to Stage 8, timing and narrative-structure to Stage 7, and dialogue-audio to Stage 9. The optional description is cleared and not stored (wave-1 CAP-0280). No issue type returns to Stage 10 frames.
notes: Relevant to the review routing idea AV-049.

title: Inpaint canvas offers brush and eraser tools only
summary: InpaintCanvas declares tool type 'brush' | 'eraser' with brush default. InpaintingModal is rendered at Stage10FrameGeneration.tsx:1721, so the inpaint path is reachable. No rectangle, ellipse or lasso tool exists.
notes: Mask is stored but not transmitted (wave-1 FACT-0189).

title: voice_profile_id is a persisted free-text column on global assets with no reader
summary: Global assets have a nullable voice_profile_id TEXT column (comment: 'ElevenLabs ID or similar'). The assets CRUD route writes it on create and update. The type is declared in src/types/asset.ts. No prompt, video, frame or UI code reads it, and no voice-service client exists.
notes: Only storage; no voice behaviour exists.

title: Shot-duration validator accepts 1 to 30 seconds; the Veo provider silently clamps to 4, 6 or 8
summary: shotValidationService errors above 30 seconds and warns above 12. Stage 7 extraction defaults to 8 seconds. Veo3Provider clamps any requested duration to the nearest of 4, 6 or 8 with a log line only. Cost is computed from the unclamped shot duration (wave-1 FACT-0127), and the validator never requires a split for shots longer than 8 seconds.
notes: shotValidation.test.ts covers the validator thresholds; the provider clamp is not tested.

title: Reference images are not capped: every reference URL is sent to the provider
summary: executeJobInBackground prepends every referenceImageUrls entry to the provider's reference list with no count limit. No maximum or budget constant appears in the image-generation, frame-generation or prompt-generation services.
notes: Quality effect of large reference sets is UNKNOWN statically.

title: Reference-image load failures fall back to text-only generation with only a console warning
summary: NanoBananaClient downloads each reference separately, counts failures, continues, and when none load proceeds with text context or the base prompt only, logging a warning. Nothing is written to the job, frame or UI, so the user is not told that references were dropped.
notes: Silent degradation path; contradicts the reference-failure surfacing idea GEN-127.

title: Use-as-reference toggle starts OFF in Stage 10 and ON in the shared upload modal used by Stage 8 scene assets
summary: FramePanel's 'Use current image as reference' switch starts false (FramePanel.tsx:170). EnhancedUploadModal's 'Use as ref' switch starts true (EnhancedUploadModal.tsx:106). VisualStateEditorPanel (Stage 8 scene-asset editor) mounts that modal for uploads (VisualStateEditorPanel.tsx:811-812).
notes: Defaults are inconsistent across regeneration points.

title: Video-prompt request omits the shot setting and the scene script
summary: generateVideoPrompt's user message contains shot id, duration, action, camera, dialogue, and foreground and background character lists, plus transformation and presence notes. It does not contain setting or the scene script excerpt. The framePrompt parameter is accepted but unused (wave-1 DEAD-0117).
notes: Limits how sound design can be inferred from scene context (AV-012).

title: Prompt length limits are warn-only in the UI; the server rejects only at the PUT limits
summary: VersionedTextarea colours the counter past warnLength and past maxLength but leaves the field editable and saveable. The PUT route rejects frame prompts over 1500 and video prompts over 1000 characters with HTTP 400. The UI limits differ again (wave-1 FACT-0115).
notes: UI never blocks save at the displayed maximum.

title: Continuity-break warning suppression is a browser localStorage flag
summary: The FramePanel break-link confirmation can be suppressed by a 'Don't show again' checkbox that writes localStorage key skipContinuityBreakConfirm; the flag is read on the next break attempt. Nothing is stored server-side.
notes: Browser-only preference; per-device.

title: Render completion is announced by in-app toast only; no email or push sender exists
summary: Stage 12 shows a success or warning toast when all jobs finish, but only while the Stage 12 component is mounted. The video executor has no notify step after completion, and no mailer or outbound notification call exists in backend/src. Scene status is recomputed in the database only.
notes: Absence of email is established by search of backend/src for mailer and send calls; the search is the evidence.

title: Character identity merges only on identical uppercase names; no alias merge
summary: Deterministic extraction keys characters by the uppercased dialogue name. The only alias handling merges case variants of the same string. Full-name and short-name variants such as 'JOHN' and 'JOHN DOE' stay separate assets.
notes: Location aliases exist only on location assets (project_assets.location_aliases). No alias logic was found for characters or props. Relevant to WD-IDEA-ASSET-046.

title: Action-line presence uses raw uppercase substring match
summary: Non-speaking character presence is set when the uppercased character key appears anywhere in an action line, with no word boundary. A short name can match inside a longer word or a different character's name.
notes: The manifest test covers dialogue counts and scene numbers; no test was found for word-boundary false positives. Impact on scene presence is not measured here.

title: Dialogue counts are computed but do not classify leads or extras
summary: Each character's dialogue line count is computed during extraction and reaches the UI only as preview mentionCount. No code path reads the count to separate main characters from one-line extras.
notes: Smoke script asserts the counts (scriptManifest.smoke.ts:80-82), which is not a jest test; the jest suite covers speakers and presence but no count assertion was found. Relevant to WD-IDEA-ASSET-041.

title: Shot-asset auto-population assigns every asset to every shot as throughout
summary: When Stage 8 or 9 loads, every missing (shot, scene instance) pair is inserted with presence_type throughout. The AssetDrawer add flow is different: it preselects heuristic matches and falls back to all shots when none match.
notes: Relevant to WD-IDEA-ASSET-204, -205, -206. Both defaults are present; the rule-based default in ASSET-206 is not the automatic one.

title: All Stage 12 export controls are disabled placeholders
summary: ExportSection renders Download MP4, YouTube, Google Drive and CapCut as buttons with no click handler, each with the disabled attribute. No export or download path for a finished video exists in the frontend.
notes: WD-IMPL-CAP-0281 lists the export options as a capability; this entry narrows it to placeholders. Relevant to WD-IDEA-PHIL-095 and -097.

title: voice_profile_id is stored on global assets and never read by generation
summary: Global asset create and update accept voiceProfileId and write voice_profile_id. No backend service or frontend component reads the field into image or video generation, so the voice seed described in the idea has no consumer.
notes: Searches: voice_profile|voiceProfile|elevenlabs across backend/src and src found only these sites. Relevant to WD-IDEA-ASSET-111.

title: Angle variants apply to characters only, including the matched-angle priority
summary: Multi-angle generation rejects non-character assets. In prompt assembly the matched angle is set only for characters; for other assets the priority is matched angle, then scene image, then master image.
notes: Relevant to WD-IDEA-ASSET-097 and -203. Props do not receive an angle variant.

title: Capsule libraries have no sharing flag; style-capsule images are public-read
summary: style_capsule_libraries has no public or shared column, and its select policy admits only the owner or preset rows. Separately, the storage policy for style-capsule images is public read for everyone.
notes: Relevant to WD-IDEA-ASSET-020 and -021. The public-read storage policy is the legacy workaround the idea describes.

title: Change Type keeps the approved image
summary: The asset_type branch of the project-asset update only sets asset_type and tracks the field. It does not clear image_key_url or attempts, so the image survives a type change.
notes: The test file covers PUT type rules; whether it asserts image retention was not checked line by line. Relevant to WD-IDEA-ASSET-106 and -107.

title: use_master_as_is defaults to FALSE in the schema
summary: The scene_asset_instances.use_master_as_is column is added with DEFAULT FALSE. Any default-checked behavior therefore has to come from UI code, which was not found to set it on creation.
notes: Relevant to WD-IDEA-ASSET-168. The UI default was not traced.

title: Upload modal has no session attempts carousel
summary: EnhancedUploadModal polls for job completion and shows the current preview, but it keeps no list of attempts from the session. The attempts carousel that exists is the persisted one in the Stage 5 and Stage 8 panels.
notes: Relevant to WD-IDEA-ASSET-124.

title: Status tags reach AI context; no tag templates, severity, conflicts or bulk tag tooling
summary: Per-instance status tags are placed into the AI context object and the scene asset payload. The tag editor offers carry-forward, but no template, severity, conflict check, history, bulk tagging or tag filter was found.
notes: Relevant to WD-IDEA-ASSET-192 through -199. Tags are not expanded into prompt phrases.

title: Any asset can be changed to extra_archetype through Change Type
summary: The PUT route validates asset_type against a list that includes extra_archetype and accepts it for any existing asset. A character can therefore become an archetype, although the idea records that path as rejected.
notes: Relevant to WD-IDEA-ASSET-076. The test file covers type changes, including cross-type merges; the archetype path was not checked specifically.

title: Script import locks Stage 4 before review and lands on Stage 5
summary: Streamline routing with a usable screenplay sets stage 1 locked, stages 2 and 3 skipped (or imported) and stage 4 locked from the imported script, then the commit lands on Stage 5 because all of stages 1-4 have transitions; the user never reviews Stage 4 as a draft first.
notes: Contradicts the product-knowledge idea that a finished script lands at Stage 4 for review (WD-IDEA-FLOW-074); the Stage 4 lock is written by the atomic commit before the user sees it.

title: Location continuity warnings require force at shot-list lock but the UI calls them advisory
summary: Unresolved, ambiguous and scene-mismatch location counts add a warning to the lock validation; the lock returns 409 unless force is set, and the Stage 7 dialog offers Lock Anyway, while the copy says these location issues are advisory.
notes: Refines WD-IMPL-INVALIDATE-0053: the title says location warnings never block, which holds only in the sense that they are overridable by one confirmation, not a hard block.

title: Skip supersedes a draft or outdated stage with empty content
summary: The Phase A skip route and the streamline_commit skip transition refuse only when the latest stage row is locked; when it is draft or outdated with real content, a new skipped version with content {} becomes the latest row.
notes: Earlier draft versions remain in stage_states history, so nothing is deleted, but the active view loses the draft; the product-knowledge rule that skip is only from not-started (WD-IDEA-FLOW-080) is not enforced. The REST skip route has no frontend caller (WD-IMPL-ROUTE-0030), so the reachable path is the Streamline commit.

title: Shot extraction folds off-screen prominence into the background list
summary: The prompt asks for foreground, background or off-screen per character, but mapCharactersToForegroundBackground stores both background and off-screen characters in charactersBackground, so off-screen status is not kept on the shot.
notes: Any unrecognized prominence value defaults to foreground (line 173-174 comment and code); test coverage for this mapping not checked.

title: Shot continuity_flags reach the frame prompt but no Stage 7 UI shows them
summary: Extraction maps the LLM continuity_flags onto each shot; the Stage 9 starting-frame prompt builder inserts them as Continuity notes for the model, but no component under src renders or edits continuity flags in the shot list.
notes: The user cannot see or edit the flags in Stage 7 (grep of src for continuityFlags and continuity_flags in .tsx files found no match); persistence of the shots column was not traced column by column.

title: Extraction prompt says exactly 8 seconds but code keeps any LLM duration from 1 to 30
summary: The system prompt requires every shot to be exactly 8 seconds unless justified, but validateShot only discards durations outside 1-30 and extraction stores the LLM duration or the default 8; no clamp or justification check exists.
notes: The 8-second rule is enforced only by the model's compliance; the shot-validation warnings for durations outside 4-12 seconds (shotValidationService.ts:127-139) apply at lock time.

title: Blocking reference roles are reserved in type unions and a label map only
summary: The reference-role unions include blocking_composition_reference, blocking_start_frame, blocking_end_frame and the source blocking_reference, and the Stage 9 preview maps them to labels, but no code path assigns any of these roles or sources.
notes: Matches the product-knowledge statement that blocking roles are reserved but not built (WD-IDEA-SHOT-105); the grep for the role strings found only type and label occurrences.

title: Stage 4 generation is gated on Stage 3 beat content, not on Stage 3 lock
summary: Stage 4 load reads the latest Stage 3 content and requires beats to be present to proceed; the Stage 3 locked status is not checked in this path, so a script can be generated from unlocked beats.
notes: The lock predecessor rule (WD-IMPL-INVALIDATE-0002) still applies when Stage 4 itself is locked; this fact is only about generation.

title: Starting-frame prompt is told to carry camera position only, with movement reserved for video
summary: The Stage 9 starting-frame prompt builder instructs the model to extract only the static camera position (shot type, angle, lens) and ignore movement, and the video prompt builder instructs it to carry movement, so one camera string feeds two prompts with a split.
notes: Adds the camera-split behaviour that the AI entries summarise without stating; the split is prompt-level instruction only, not validated after generation.

title: Manual staging accepts .doc and reads it as text
summary: The Stage 1 manual FileStagingArea accepts application/msword and reads every non-PDF file with readAsText, so a binary legacy .doc is not rejected on this path. The explicit 'save as .docx or .pdf' rejection exists only in the Streamline extraction service.
notes: Runtime output of readAsText on a binary .doc was not run; the static code has no conversion step on this path.

title: Stage 1 autosave is disabled; drafts are written only on Continue
summary: Stage 1 passes autoSave: false to the stage-state hook, with a comment that it is disabled to avoid a race with the manual lock. The draft is written only when the user presses Continue.
notes: Stage 2-4 do autosave on mount (STATE-0021); Stage 1 does not. Intake state before Continue is React state only (WD-IMPL-STATE-0032).

title: Stage 2 'Retroactively Revise Treatment' is a toast-only stub
summary: The retroactive-revision handler in Stage 2 only shows a toast reading 'Retroactive revision triggered' and does not call any service or route.
notes: The button is rendered and clickable; no regeneration from current beats occurs.

title: Beat treatment-excerpt view is never populated
summary: Beats declare an originalTreatmentExcerpt field and Stage 3 renders an expandable 'View original treatment context' block for it, but no code in src assigns that field, so the block never appears.
notes: Searched for assignments to originalTreatmentExcerpt in src/ and backend/src/; the only hits are the type declaration and the render site.

title: Aspect ratio has two values and can be changed at any stage
summary: The AspectRatio type and the PUT validator allow only 16:9 and 9:16, and the project update route accepts aspect_ratio with no check on stage lock state, so the setting is editable after Stage 2 has begun.
notes: The aspect ratio chip is shown in the project header (CAP-0052); whether any other code treats the value as locked was not traced.

title: Stage 1 option sets are fixed in the UI
summary: Stage 1 offers exactly 10 genres, 4 content ratings (G, PG, PG-13, M), 3 project types (narrative, commercial, 'Video for Audio'), and a 1-15 minute target-length slider. Any other value cannot be chosen in the UI.
notes: The audio-visual option is selectable but rejected by the backend (FACT-0046).

title: Stage 4 scene preview shows only number, heading, slug and opening action
summary: The Stage 4 preview dialog renders each previewed scene's number, header or slug, and opening action (or a 150-character excerpt). It does not show characters, location, or props, which the preview idea names.
notes: The preview is in-memory only (sceneService.previewScenes); no persistence occurs.

title: Streamline raw uploads are never stored; only routed text enters stage content
summary: Streamline documents are held in multer memory storage and only their extracted text is returned to the browser. The commit payload carries stage transitions, project config, Stage 1 draft, asset drafts, and resolutions, not the source files. Only staged reference images are uploaded to storage.
notes: Stage content holds the routed text (as-is or AI-formatted), so the words survive but the original file does not. Source-file traceability (INPUT-066) is therefore absent.

title: Unclassified and non-routed intake files drop out at routing and commit
summary: computeStreamlineRouting creates lines and stage transitions only for scripts, treatments, beat sheets, character/location notes and images. Files of any other or unclassified type produce no routing line and are not in the commit payload.
notes: Contradicts the 'unclassified files are kept as context, never discarded' idea. Routing tests exist (streamlineRouting.test.ts) but no test was found asserting that unclassified files are retained.

title: Writing style capsule text is injected only into the treatment, beat and master-script templates
summary: The {writing_style_context} placeholder appears only in the treatment_expansion, beat_extraction and master_script_generation seed templates. No Stage 7 or Stage 9 prompt builder in backend/src references writing capsules.
notes: Covers Stages 2-4 only; the idea's Stages 7 and 9 are not covered. Shot and prompt services were searched for writingStyle/writing_style (no hits).

title: Stage-specific context assembler has no production callers
summary: ContextManager.prepareStageContext, assembleFullContext and formatPromptGenerationContext have no callers outside tests. formatForInjection is called in production only by the Streamline backfill service.
notes: The only test referencing prepareStageContext is backend/src/tests/contextManagerAuteurResolutions.test.ts. Generation routes build prompt context inline in llm.ts.

title: Ask Auteur has four question categories and two-to-four options
summary: The Ask Auteur question schema allows four categories (contradiction, vague_trait, ambiguous_structure, missing_info) and instructs the model to produce 2-4 options per question. There is no separate conflict-resolution category.
notes: A streamlineQuestion.test.ts exists; it was not read for category coverage.

title: New beats default to 20 seconds and fallback beats to 60 seconds
summary: Adding a beat in the UI assigns estimatedScreenTimeSeconds 20. When the beat-sheet response cannot be parsed, the fallback beat uses 60 seconds. No control exists to change a beat's duration.
notes: Duration is displayed (Stage3BeatSheet.tsx:178) but is not editable in the beat sheet.

title: Beat-sheet narrative_structure is parsed and stored but never rendered
summary: The beat parser reads narrative_structure from the model output (default '3-act structure') and it is carried in Stage 3 content. No component renders it.
notes: Searched Stage3BeatSheet.tsx and related components for 'structure' display; only the type and assignment lines match.
